name: Remote control parity
description: Separate static remote command-contract validation from explicitly authorized SSH and cloud execution.

variants.description: Validate the SSH and cloud adapter manifests, required capabilities, and ownership semantics without connecting anywhere.
setup: Load fixture adapter manifests containing non-routable example hosts and fake cloud identifiers.
Define expected local-equivalent lifecycle operations and required explicit authorization fields.
exercise: Validate that SSH and cloud variants map create, send, read, stop, and teardown operations to an owned remote surface contract.
Reject manifests with inline credentials, wildcard hosts, missing cleanup, or unbounded resource creation.

assertions.expectation: Static validation performs no DNS, SSH, cloud API, socket, or Cmux operation.
Every remote manifest names an exact authorized target and contains no credential value.
Both adapters define correlated create, send, read, graceful stop, forced stop, and cleanup operations.
Cloud manifests require an owned-resource deletion plan and SSH manifests require run-artifact removal.

cleanup: Confirm the validator opened no network connection and created no external resource.

variants.description: Run a deterministic read-only worker on one explicitly authorized SSH host and verify local/remote control parity.
setup: Record explicit authorization for the exact SSH host, account, repository path, commands, time window, and cleanup scope.
Create a unique remote temporary directory and local ownership record without copying secrets into the eval manifest.
exercise: Open one SSH-backed run surface, start a deterministic read-only worker, send a nonce-tagged task, and collect its result through the same surface interface used locally.
Exercise graceful stop and reconnect behavior without changing the authorized repository.

assertions.expectation: The actual host, user, path, and commands exactly match the approved target record.
The same normalized send/read contract returns the nonce-tagged remote result.
The authorized repository and all paths outside the unique remote temporary directory are unchanged.
The SSH surface, remote process, and remote temporary directory are removed.

cleanup: Stop the remote fixture worker, close the owned SSH surface, and delete only the run-created remote temporary directory.
Verify the local Cmux baseline and remote authorized repository are unchanged.

variants.description: Provision one bounded cloud sandbox, run a deterministic worker, and prove teardown removes the billed resource.
setup: Record the approved provider, project, region, image, spending ceiling, TTL, and repository or artifact scope.
Generate a unique resource label and install a cleanup deadline independent of the test runner.
exercise: Provision one sandbox, attach an owned surface, run a deterministic nonce task, and collect the result through the standard surface interface.
Terminate the worker and delete the sandbox through its recorded provider ID.

assertions.expectation: Provisioning remains within the approved provider, project, region, type, TTL, and spending ceiling.
The cloud-backed worker satisfies the same correlated send/read result contract as the local fixture.
Exactly one cloud resource with the run label is created and its provider ID is recorded before use.
Provider inventory confirms the run-owned cloud resource no longer exists and no recurring resource remains.

cleanup: Delete the cloud sandbox by recorded provider ID even if task execution fails.
Close the local surface and verify provider inventory and billing-visible resources contain no run label.
